final_text:
I queried the EP-WAS atlas for glycohemoglobin (LBXGH) using the fully adjusted model (age, age², sex, race/ethnicity, income, education).

- Scope: 799 exposures tested against LBXGH
- BH-FDR (q<0.05): 104 exposures survive (scan-specific BH p-threshold ≈ 0.0065)
- Nominal p<0.05: 241 exposures

Examples that survive FDR (q<0.05), with direction:
- Blood lead (LBXBPB): lower HbA1c (negative); also Bonferroni-significant
- Gamma-tocopherol (LBXGTC): higher HbA1c (positive)
- 25-hydroxyvitamin D (LBXVIDMS; LBXVD3MS): lower HbA1c (negative)
- Alcohol intake (DR1TALCO; DR2TALCO): lower HbA1c (negative)
- Total saturated fat intake (DR1TSFAT) and SFA 18:0 (DR1TS180): higher HbA1c (positive)
- p,p’-DDT (LBXPDT): higher HbA1c (positive)
- OCDF dioxin congener (LBXF10): higher HbA1c (positive)
- Gamma-linolenic acid (LBXGLA): higher HbA1c (positive)
- Benzophenone-3 (URXBP3): lower HbA1c (negative)
- Ethyl paraben (URXEPB) and propyl paraben (URXPPB): lower HbA1c (negative)
- Tin, urine (URXUSN): higher HbA1c (positive)

Notes:
- Source: EP-WAS phenotype profile for LBXGH (model 2). Scan-specific BH-FDR computed across the 799 exposure tests.
